Title: Webhooks
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/api-documentation/webhooks
Content: All webhooks that have been configured on an account are listed on the Webhooks page. You will see the name of the webhook, the recipient URL, the event types that trigger the webhook, and options to manage or delete the webhook.

You will also see a toggle next to the recipient URL that switches the webhook on or off.

Click Manage to open a new dialogue that you can use to edit, review, and test your webhook. The SUMMARY tab is used to edit webhook names, reciepient URLs, and event types that trigger the webhook. The CONNECTIVITY tab allows you to test a webhook and view the JSON request payload and response.

The HISTORY tab stores requests and responses for 7 days. This history is especially useful for troubleshooting any failed requests, and failed requests can be easily found by looking for the red X on the left of an entry. You can also view the request payload and response of any webhook here.
Title: Service accounts
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/connectors/connectors-overview/service-accounts
Content: Webhooks are HTTP POST requests containing a JSON payload that are sent to a third-party URL separately configured to receive them.

Webhooks can be used as external notifications or triggers for events in external systems. Configuring webhooks on service accounts is an effective way to monitor the automated activity of connectors on any models the service account has access to.

See webhooks for more information and instructions for setting up webhooks.
